items.new: 39-section omnibus (AEDT/employment AI incl. WARN-notice AI disclosure, companion chatbots, provenance, social media, regulatory sandbox). Frontier-relevant sections: frontier developers may not retaliate against covered employees reporting catastrophic-risk concerns or adopt contracts barring such reporting (effective Oct. 1, 2026); large frontier developers must operate anonymous internal reporting channels by Jan. 1, 2027, with quarterly sharing of reports with officers and directors; frontier developers must give covered employees notice of their rights; civil penalty up to $1,000 per violation of subsections (b) to (d), in an AG action in Hartford superior court, with state recovery of investigation costs and attorneys' fees when prevailing; plus a DCP-run IVO pilot through June 30, 2030 — see Section C.
items.note: self-correction (omission): The penalty covers all of subsections (b) to (d), including the employee-notice duty, not only the whistleblower duties, and the state can recover investigation costs and attorneys' fees. The entry also ends with a 'does not contain' statement, which the rules forbid. Quote: "Any frontier developer that violates any provision of subsections"

items.old: A Department of Consumer Protection-administered IVO pilot program (Sec. 33, effective July 1, 2027) through June 30, 2030 (no more than five IVOs, each under a memorandum of understanding): IVO applications and designation standards, annual reporting, reassessment and suspension, public transparency, and rules for the evidentiary treatment of verification in private litigation (admissible solely in private personal-injury or property-damage actions; not in AG or state-agency enforcement actions). DCP must evaluate the pilot by Dec. 31, 2028 with UConn's Institute for Municipal and Regional Policy. This is an operating pilot, not merely a study
items.new: A Department of Consumer Protection-administered IVO pilot program (Sec. 33, effective July 1, 2027) through June 30, 2030 (no more than five IVOs, each under a memorandum of understanding): IVO applications and designation standards, annual reporting, reassessment and suspension, public transparency, and rules for the evidentiary treatment of verification in private litigation (admissible solely in private personal-injury or property-damage actions; not in AG or state-agency enforcement actions, nor presumption, inference or defense there). Except: wilful, wanton or reckless conduct; misrepresentation; failure to implement corrective action. DCP must evaluate the pilot by Dec. 31, 2028 with UConn's Institute for Municipal and Regional Policy. This is an operating pilot, not merely a study
items.note: self-correction (omission): The entry omits that the evidence rule bars any presumption, inference or defense from verification in AG or state-agency actions, and omits the exceptions that remove the evidentiary limit for wilful, wanton or reckless conduct, material misrepresentation, or failure to implement required corrective action. Quote: "nor shall it give rise to any presumption, inference or defense in any such action"

items.old: Frontier AI framework; risk reports every 180 days; critical safety incidents reported to AG within 15 days (24 hours if imminent risk of death); annual independent third-party audit; AG civil-action enforcement, up to $1,000,000 first violation, $3,000,000 subsequent; Senate version: mandatory independent third-party catastrophic-risk review at least every 120 days (the most frequent evaluation cadence among the bills reviewed); whistleblower protections; commission on further AI regulation. Chapter 93M effective July 1, 2027. House version (passed July 8) contains no AI-safety language — only funding.
items.new: Frontier AI framework; risk reports every 180 days; critical safety incidents reported to AG within 15 days (24 hours if imminent risk of death); annual independent third-party audit; AG civil-action enforcement, up to $1,000,000 first violation, $3,000,000 subsequent; Senate version: mandatory independent third-party catastrophic-risk review at least every 120 days (the most frequent evaluation cadence among the bills reviewed); whistleblower protections (covered employees may petition superior court for injunctive relief; court may award attorney's fees and court costs to a successful plaintiff); commission on further AI regulation. Chapter 93M effective July 1, 2027. House version (passed July 8) contains no AI-safety language — only funding.
